subject: BlueWave pilot: infra ownership, constraints, and go/no-go checklist
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Kate Lin <kate@bluewavehealth.com>
Date: 2028-09-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: BlueWave pilot: infra ownership, constraints, and go/no-go checklist

Team —

BlueWave confirmed next-week pilot dates (window: Oct 2–9) and wants an explicit list of what Redwood will run vs what BlueWave must provide for a Private (VPC) + on-prem data ingress pattern. I pulled together the customer ask and a rough SoW; attaching network sketch and the draft SoW for context (pilot_network_layout_v1.pdf, bluewave_sow_r1.docx).

High level asks from BlueWave:
- Private control plane in their VPC with peered connectivity to an on-prem edge for sensitive PHI processing
- Customer-managed KMS and audit log retention policy of 7 years
- SSO via Okta + SCIM provisioning

What I need from this thread: clear ownership matrix (who does what for pilot), a minimum viable acceptance checklist to hit by Oct 2, and any fatal blockers that would push the pilot timeline.

Quick thoughts:
- Karthik: are there kernel/runtime features we *must* lock down per the on-prem edges (quantization, KV caching constraints)?
- Kimberly: compliance gaps re: KMS/HSM and retention — are these pilot-level mitigations acceptable or do we need an exception?
- Soojin/Dev/Grace: staffing — how many on-call hours and who needs escalation privileges during the pilot?

I propose a 30-minute sync tomorrow 9:30am PT; if you can’t make it, reply with bullets and owner assignments.

Thanks —
Jordan
Jordan Blake
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Kate Lin <kate@bluewavehealth.com>
Date: 2028-09-18T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: BlueWave pilot: infra ownership, constraints, and go/no-go checklist

Thanks Jordan — quick technical read from my side. I scanned the pilot_network_layout_v1.pdf and flagged a few items:

1) KV cache & prefix caching:
- If the on-prem edge performs tokenization or partial inference, we must ensure the KV cache is not duplicated across isolated environments. For pilot simplicity, recommend we run inference entirely inside the on-prem edge box (no remote KV cross-traffic). That requires a minimal runtime build (tag: v2028-09-edge-lite) — affects package delivery but is achievable this sprint.

2) Model variant & quantization:
- BlueWave wants 8-bit performance on A100-equivalent hardware — we need to confirm the physical node supports bf16 or convert workflow to int8 quant. I marked JIRA-BACKLOG-2987 for model-quantization validation. If nodes are CPU-only, we cannot meet latency SLO.

3) Networking:
- Mutual TLS between control plane and on-prem edge is mandatory. If BlueWave insists on private peering with no egress to our hosted controllers, we must ship a temporary control-plane appliance that lives in their VPC (container + small EC2). That increases infra ops scope for the pilot.

Blocking items (need answers by EOD tomorrow):
- Hardware spec confirmation from BlueWave (GPU type, NIC bandwidth)
- Whether they will allow a Redwood-managed control-plane appliance in their VPC for the pilot or insist on full customer-managed control plane.

I can prepare a minimal runtime branch and a short checklist for the image if we confirm hardware today.

—Karthik
Senior Infrastructure Architect

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Kate Lin <kate@bluewavehealth.com>
Date: 2028-09-18T11:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: BlueWave pilot: infra ownership, constraints, and go/no-go checklist

Jordan, team —

Compliance view: pilot can proceed with mitigations but we must capture exceptions and get formal sign-off from BlueWave security for these items:

- KMS/HSM: BlueWave must either supply an HSM-backed key or accept a delegated key-in-transit model where Redwood rotates ephemeral keys. For the pilot, an ephemeral key rotation window (24 hours) is acceptable if BlueWave signs the exception attestation.
- Audit logs: we can stream audit logs to BlueWave’s S3-compliant bucket. Retention of 7 years is supported but requires lifecycle rules on their object store; we need the bucket ARN and access policy.
- Data residency: any PHI cannot leave the on-prem edge. Confirm that inference outputs classified as PHI will remain in their VLAN and be forwarded only to BlueWave-controlled endpoints.

Deliverables I need before pilot start:
1) Signed exception attestation (if ephemeral keys used) — template linked: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1BXxPilot/bluewave-docs
2) Bucket ARN and IAM principal for log writes
3) Okta/SCIM test account to validate SSO flows (SCIM provisioning for pilot users) — See attached sso_requirements.xlsx

If any of these are not provided, we must convert the pilot to an internal demo (hosted) rather than on-prem.

—Kimberly
Head of Security & Compliance

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-09-19T09:34:00-07:00
Subject: Re: BlueWave pilot: infra ownership, constraints, and go/no-go checklist

Quick operational note following yesterday’s readout and a short ops sync:

Staffing and escalation plan (pilot Oct 2–9):
- Primary on-call: Dev Patel (lead) — 8am–6pm PT daily for pilot window.
- Secondary on-call: Grace O'Connor — 6pm–2am PT for late issues and handover.
- On-call rotations will be paid OOO credit per standard pilot policy.
- We need one platform engineer onsite (remote) for the first two days for image troubleshooting (estimated 12–16 hours total).

Operational constraints that *may* change scope:
- We cannot guarantee patch-level kernel modifications during the pilot; any kernel-level tuning on customer nodes requires at least a 2-week change window and a signed operations SLA.
- Deployment-only appliance in their VPC is doable but requires a temporary IAM role and an architecture review (3 business days).

Proposed go/no-go acceptance checklist (minimal):
1) Hardware spec confirmation and access creds to test node.
2) Okta test account provisioned and SSO smoke passes.
3) Audit-log target and write policy validated.
4) Control-plane connectivity model agreed (Redwood-managed appliance OR customer-controlled with documented escalation).
5) Signed pilot SoW (bluewave_sow_r1.docx) or written email acceptance from BlueWave security.

If we cannot hit all five by Sep 26 EOD, we should move the pilot start to Oct 16 to avoid wasted on-call time.

I’ll update JIRA-BACKLOG-2987 with staffing notes and link runbook drafts to the drive folder.

—Soojin
Sr. Program Manager, Operations

Thanks — good, actionable items.

1) We will accept the ephemeral-key exception for the pilot only if BlueWave signs the attestation; Kimberly to prepare attestation template and forward to Kate by EOD tomorrow.
2) Redwood will provide a temporary control-plane appliance in BlueWave’s VPC for the pilot (checked with infra leadership). Karthik: please prepare the v2028-09-edge-lite image and the deployment runbook; Soojin/Dev — please estimate the engineer-day cost and confirm who will perform the first-day image push.

Action items and owners (short):
- Kimberly: attestation template + retention policy confirmation (owner: kimberly_park)
- Karthik: runtime build + appliance runbook + JIRA-BACKLOG-2987 update (owner: karthik_iyer)
- Soojin: finalize on-call roster & cost estimate (owner: soojin_lee)
- Dev: prepare image deployment playbook and coordinate with BlueWave net team (owner: dev_patel)
- Jordan: send pilot kickoff email and calendar invite once items 1–4 are satisfied.

Kate — appreciate your flexibility. Can you confirm the hardware spec and whether BlueWave will accept the temporary appliance in their VPC by EOD Sep 21? If you prefer a short call instead of email, I can set one.

Best —
Jordan
